source_text: Ὅθεν καὶ θανάτου γεύεται ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ διὰ τὸν σαρκικὸν αὐτοῦ πατέρα, ἵνα οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τῆς ζωῆς τοῦ Θεοῦ μεταλάβωσι, διὰ τὸν κατὰ Πνεῦμα αὐτῶν Πατέρα Θεόν· Αὐτὸς οὖν κατὰ φύσιν Υἱός ἐστι τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἡμεῖς δὲ κατὰ χάριν. Καὶ πάλιν αὐτὸς κατ' οἰκονομίαν καὶ χάριν ἡμετέραν υἱὸς γέγονε τοῦ Ἀδὰμ, ἡμεῖς δὲ κατὰ φύσιν ἐσμὲν υἱοὶ τοῦ Ἀδάμ. Ὅθεν λέγει, Ἀπέρχομαι πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα μου καὶ Πατέρα ὑμῶν, καὶ Θεόν μου, καὶ Θεὸν ὑμῶν. Πατὴρ γὰρ αὐτοῦ ἐστιν ὁ Θεὸς, ὡς προεῖπον, κατὰ φύσιν, ἡμῶν δὲ κατὰ χάριν· καὶ Θεὸς αὐτοῦ γέγονε κατ' οἰκονομίαν, διότι ἄνθρωπος, ἡμῶν δὲ κατὰ φύσιν Δεσπότης ἐστὶ καὶ Θεός. Καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ὁ Λόγος καὶ Υἱὸς τοῦ Πατρὸς ἑνωθεὶς σαρκὶ, γέγονε σὰρξ, ἄνθρωπος τέλειος, ἵνα οἱ ἄνθρωποι ἑνωθέντες Πνεύματι, γένωνται ἓν Πνεῦμα. Αὐτὸς οὖν ἐστι Θεὸς σαρκοφόρος, καὶ ἡμεῖς ἄνθρωποι πνευματοφόροι. Ἀπαρχὴν γὰρ λαβὼν ἐκ τῆς οὐσίας τῶν ἀνθρώπων, τουτέστιν ἐκ τοῦ σπέρματος Ἀδὰμ (ἥτις ἐστὶ μορφὴ δούλου), 997 καὶ ἐν ὁμοιώματι ἀνθρώπου γεγονὼς, ἔδωκεν ἡμῖν ἐκ τῆς οὐσίας τοῦ Πατρὸς, ἀπαρχὴν ἁγίου Πνεύματος· ἵνα γενώμεθα οἱ πάντες εἰς υἱοὺς Θεοῦ, ἐν ὁμοιώματι τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ Θεοῦ. Αὐτὸς οὖν ὁ ἀληθινὸς καὶ φύσει Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ τοὺς πάντας ἡμᾶς φορεῖ, ἵνα οἱ πάντες τὸν ἕνα φορέσωμεν Θεόν. Ἀσεβὲς οὖν ἐστι κτιστὸν ἢ ποιητὸν λέγειν τὸ Πνεῦμα τοῦ Θεοῦ· ὁπότε πᾶσα Γραφὴ Παλαιά τε καὶ Καινὴ, μετὰ Πατρὸς καὶ Υἱοῦ αὐτὸ συναριθμεῖ καὶ δοξάζει· διότι τῆς αὐτῆς θεότητός ἐστι, καὶ τῆς αὐτῆς ἐξουσίας· καθὼς αὐτὸς ὁ Κύριος λέγει· Ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ, ποταμοὶ ἐκ τῆς κοιλίας αὐτοῦ ῥεύσουσιν ὕδατος ζῶντος. Τοῦτο δὲ εἶπε περὶ τοῦ Πνεύματος, οὗ ἔμελλον λαμβάνειν οἱ πιστεύοντες εἰς αὐτόν· ὡς καὶ ἐν τῷ Ἰωὴλ ἐκ προσώπου τοῦ Πατρὸς λέγει· Ἐκχεῶ ἀπὸ τοῦ Πνεύματός μου ἐπὶ πᾶσαν σάρκα, καὶ προφητεύσουσιν οἱ υἱοὶ ὑμῶν καὶ αἱ θυγατέρες ὑμῶν. Καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ἐμφυσᾷ αὐτὸ εἰς τὸ πρόσωπον τῶν ἀποστόλων λέγων· Λάβετε Πνεῦμα ἅγιον· ἵνα μάθωμεν, ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ πληρώματος τῆς θεότητός ἐστι τὸ διδόμενον Πνεῦμα τοῖς μαθηταῖς. Ἐν Χριστῷ γὰρ, φησὶ, κατοικεῖ, τουτέστιν ἐν τῇ σαρκὶ αὐτοῦ, πᾶν τὸ πλήρωμα τῆς θεότητος σωματικῶς· καθὼς καὶ ὁ Βαπτιστὴς Ἰωάννης λέγει· Ἡμεῖς πάντες ἐκ τοῦ πληρώματος αὐτοῦ ἐλάβομεν. Σωματικῷ γὰρ εἴδει, τουτέστιν ὡς περιστερὰ, ὤφθη τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, καταβαῖνον καὶ μένον ἐπ' αὐτόν. Ἐν ἡμῖν μὲν γὰρ ἀπαρχὴ καὶ ἀῤῥαβὼν θεότητος κατοικεῖ, ἐν Χριστῷ δὲ πᾶν τὸ πλήρωμα τῆς θεότητος. Καὶ μή τις νομίσῃ, ὅτι μὴ ἔχων αὐτὸ ἐλάμβανεν· αὐτὸς γὰρ αὐτὸ ἄνωθεν ἔπεμπεν, ὡς Θεός· καὶ αὐτὸς αὐτὸ κάτω ὑπεδέχετο, ὡς ἄνθρωπος. Ἐξ αὐτοῦ οὖν εἰς αὐτὸν κατῄει, ἐκ τῆς θεότητος αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν ἀνθρωπότητα αὐτοῦ. Καὶ ὁ μὲν Ἡσαΐας ἐκ προσώπου τοῦ Πατρὸς βοᾷ λέγων· Οὕτω λέγει Κύριος ὁ Θεός σου, ὁ ποιήσας σε καὶ πλάσας σε ἐκ κοιλίας· Μὴ φοβοῦ, ὁ παῖς μου Ἰακὼβ, καὶ ὁ ἠγαπημένος Ἰσραὴλ, ὃν ἐξελεξάμην· ὅτι ἐγὼ δώσω ὕδωρ ἐν δίψει τοῖς πορευομένοις ἐν ἀνύδρῳ· ἐπιθήσω τὸ Πνεῦμά μου ἐπὶ τὸ σπέρμα σου, καὶ τὰς εὐλογίας μου ἐπὶ τὰ τέκνα σου.
thought_title: The Son's fleshly sonship and the Spirit's divinity
orientation: Marcellus continues his argument that the Son's human sonship is by the plan of salvation while his divine sonship is by nature, and he now turns to the divinity of the Holy Spirit.
pass_a_gloss: Wherefore also of death tastes the Son of God because of the fleshly of him father, in order that the sons of the man of the life of God may share, because of the according to Spirit of them Father God; He therefore according to nature Son is of God, we but according to grace. And again he according to dispensation and grace our son became of Adam, we but according to nature are sons of Adam. Wherefore he says, I go away to the Father of me and Father of you, and God of me, and God of you. Father for of him is God, as I said before, according to nature, of us but according to grace; and God of him became according to dispensation, because man, of us but according to nature Master is and God. And because of this the Word and Son of the Father having been united to flesh, became flesh, man perfect, in order that the men having been united to Spirit, may become one Spirit. He therefore is God flesh-bearing, and we men spirit-bearing. First-fruit for having taken from the substance of the men, that is from the seed of Adam (which is form of slave), 997 and in likeness of man having become, he gave to us from the substance of the Father, first-fruit of holy Spirit; in order that we may become all into sons of God, in likeness of the Son of God. He therefore the true and by nature Son of God all us wears, in order that all the one may wear God. Impious therefore it is created or made to say the Spirit of God; seeing that all Scripture Old both and New, with Father and Son it numbers together and glorifies; because of the same divinity it is, and of the same authority; just as himself the Lord says: The one believing in me, rivers from the belly of him will flow of water living. This but he said about the Spirit, which they were about to receive the ones believing in him; as also in Joel from person of the Father he says: I will pour out from the Spirit of me upon all flesh, and they will prophesy the sons of you and the daughters of you. And because of this he breathes it into the face of the apostles saying: Receive Spirit holy; in order that we may learn, that from the fullness of the divinity is the being given Spirit to the disciples. In Christ for, he says, dwells, that is in the flesh of him, all the fullness of the divinity bodily; just as also the Baptist John says: We all from the fullness of him received. In bodily for form, that is as dove, was seen the Spirit the holy, coming down and remaining upon him. In us for first-fruit and pledge of divinity dwells, in Christ but all the fullness of the divinity. And not anyone may think, that not having it he was receiving; he for it from above was sending, as God; and he it below was receiving, as man. From him therefore into him it was coming down, from the divinity of him into the humanity of him. And the Isaiah from person of the Father cries out saying: Thus says Lord the God of you, the one having made you and formed you from womb; Do not fear, the servant of me Jacob, and the beloved Israel, whom I chose; because I will give water in thirst to the ones going in waterless; I will put the Spirit of me upon the seed of you, and the blessings of me upon the children of you.

pass_b_english: So the Son of God also tastes death because of his fleshly father, so that the sons of man might share in the life of God because of their Father according to the Spirit, God. He is therefore Son of God by nature, but we are sons by grace. And again, he became a son of Adam by the plan of salvation and for our sake, while we are sons of Adam by nature. Therefore he says, “I am going to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God” (John 20:17). For God is his Father, as I said before, by nature, but ours by grace; and God became his God by the plan of salvation, because he is man, but for us he is by nature Master and God. And for this reason the Word and Son of the Father, united to flesh, became flesh, a complete man, so that human beings, united to the Spirit, might become one Spirit. He therefore is God bearing flesh, and we are human beings bearing Spirit. For he took firstfruits from the substance of human beings, that is, from the seed of Adam—which is the form of a servant—and having come in the likeness of a human being, he gave us from the substance of the Father a firstfruits of the Holy Spirit, so that we might all become sons of God in the likeness of the Son of God. He therefore, the true and natural Son of God, bears all of us, so that all of us might carry the one God. It is therefore impious to call the Spirit of God a creature or something made, when all Scripture, both Old and New, numbers and glorifies it together with the Father and the Son, because it is of the same divinity and the same authority. As the Lord himself says, “Whoever believes in me, rivers of living water will flow from his belly” (John 7:38). He said this about the Spirit, which those who believed in him were about to receive (John 7:39). As he also says in Joel, in the person of the Father, “I will pour out from my Spirit on all flesh, and your sons and your daughters will prophesy” (Joel 2:28). And for this reason he breathes it into the face of the apostles, saying, “Receive the Holy Spirit” (John 20:22), so that we might learn that the Spirit given to the disciples is from the fullness of deity. For in Christ, he says—that is, in his flesh—all the fullness of deity dwells bodily (Colossians 2:9). As John the Baptist also says, “We have all received from his fullness” (John 1:16). For the Holy Spirit appeared in bodily form, that is, as a dove, descending and remaining on him. In us dwells a firstfruits and guarantee of deity, but in Christ all the fullness of deity. And let no one suppose that he received it though he did not have it; for he himself sent it from above, as God, and he himself received it below, as man. From himself, therefore, it descended into himself—from his divinity into his humanity. And Isaiah cries out in the person of the Father, saying, “Thus says the Lord your God, who made you and formed you from the womb: Do not fear, my servant Jacob, and beloved Israel, whom I have chosen; for I will give water in thirst to those who walk in a waterless land; I will put my Spirit upon your seed, and my blessings upon your children” (Isaiah 44:2-3).
notes: The numeral 997 appears in the source text after μορφὴ δούλου; it is likely a page or folio number and is not translated.

problems.why: σαρκικὸν πατέρα means 'fleshly father' in sense of human father/Adam, not 'because of' but 'for the sake of'
problems.fix: for the sake of his fleshly father, that is, Adam

problems.quote: by the plan of salvation and for our sake
problems.why: χάριν ἡμετέραν = 'for our grace' or 'by our grace', not 'for our sake'; καὶ links two datives of manner/means
problems.fix: by the plan of salvation and by our grace
problems.ruling: χάριν ἡμετέραν is 'our grace', not 'for our sake'; κατ' οἰκονομίαν καὶ χάριν are parallel.

problems.quote: he gave us from the substance of the Father the firstfruits of the Holy Spirit
problems.source_quote: ἔδωκεν ἡμῖν ἐκ τῆς οὐσίας τοῦ Πατρὸς, ἀπαρχὴν ἁγίου Πνεύματος
problems.why: ἀπαρχὴν is in apposition to what was given, not 'firstfruits of the Holy Spirit' but 'firstfruits, [namely] Holy Spirit' or 'firstfruits which is the Holy Spirit'
problems.fix: he gave us from the substance of the Father a firstfruits, the Holy Spirit
problems.ruling: ἀπαρχὴν ἁγίου Πνεύματος is appositional: 'firstfruits, [namely] Holy Spirit', not 'of the Holy Spirit'.

problems.quote: he received it because he did not have it
problems.why: μὴ ἔχων = 'not having it', but the Greek says he received it though not having it (participial concession); English 'because' makes it causal, but it's concessive/contrastive
problems.fix: he received it though he did not have it
problems.ruling: ὅτι μὴ ἔχων αὐτὸ ἐλάμβανεν is concessive: 'received it though not having it', not 'because he did not have it'.

Changed 'and for our sake' to 'and by our grace' (χάριν ἡμετέραν is a dative of means, not 'for our sake').

problems.quote: for the sake of his fleshly father
problems.why: σαρκικὸν πατέρα means 'fleshly father' (Adam), not 'for the sake of his fleshly father'. διὰ here means 'on account of/because of', not 'for the sake of' in a benefactive sense; the Son tastes death because he has a fleshly father (Adam), not to benefit Adam.
problems.fix: because of his fleshly father, or on account of his fleshly father

problems.why: φορέσωμεν means 'might carry' or 'might bear', but in context this is about wearing/bearing God within us, not 'bearing' in the sense of enduring. 'Bear' is ambiguous in English between 'carry' and 'endure'.
problems.fix: might carry the one God, or might bear the one God within us

problems.why: χάριν ἡμετέραν means 'for our sake' or 'for our benefit', not 'by our grace'. The grace is God's, not ours; the Son became son of Adam for our benefit.
problems.fix: for our sake, or for our benefit
problems.ruling: χάριν ἡμετέραν = 'for our sake/benefit,' not 'by our grace'; grace is God's, not ours.

problems.quote: he gave us from the substance of the Father a firstfruits, the Holy Spirit
problems.source_quote: ἔδωκεν ἡμῖν ἐκ τῆς οὐσίας τοῦ Πατρὸς, ἀπαρχὴν ἁγίου Πνεύματος
problems.why: ἀπαρχὴν ἁγίου Πνεύματος is 'a firstfruits of Holy Spirit' (partitive genitive), not 'a firstfruits, the Holy Spirit' in apposition. The Spirit itself is not called the firstfruits; rather, what is given is a firstfruits/portions of the Spirit.
problems.fix: he gave us from the substance of the Father a firstfruits of the Holy Spirit
problems.ruling: ἀπαρχὴν ἁγίου Πνεύματος is partitive genitive 'firstfruits OF Holy Spirit,' not apposition 'firstfruits, the Holy Spirit.'
